completeness.why: copyPreviousMonth delegates its skip decision to shouldIncludeMonthBudgetCategory('copy-previous', ...); setZero and the three averages take their category set from getMonthBudgetCategories with an action argument; both sign inversions go through averageToBudgetAmount. No site keeps its own filter, income check or sign branch.

interface.why: The action enum is a reasonable way to name the zero-vs-average variation (setZero writes hidden categories), but getMonthBudgetCategories has a 'copy-previous' branch and an optional previousMonth parameter that no caller uses (copyPreviousMonth keeps getBudgetData). For averages the hidden rule is applied twice, once in the SQL and again in the predicate. The missing-group (NULL group_hidden) inconsistency is not made explicit; the predicate treats it the same as hidden for copy-previous.

disguised_duplication.where: month-action-categories.ts: the 'average' SQL keeps 'c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0' while shouldIncludeMonthBudgetCategory re-checks hidden/group_hidden, so the same rule exists in SQL and in JS; the unused 'copy-previous' query re-creates getBudgetData's budget-table join in another form
